replies.body: Raised the module baseline and Muzzle range to stable 4.0.0 in [`7ccf5c5`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/commit/7ccf5c54238c4c7f56e93a793640c0796bcd15c4). The PR description records why beta1 was originally used and that Muzzle does not sample prereleases.

Removed this `@NoMuzzle` path in [`7ccf5c5`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/commit/7ccf5c54238c4c7f56e93a793640c0796bcd15c4) by using the stable `ConnectionProvider` carrier directly; the reflective carrier lookup and manual registrations are gone.

Kept `isDeclaredBy` because `TopologyRefreshTask` has the same `run()` signature, and added the explanation in [`6925d5d`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/commit/6925d5dbc7c1fdd165223b82057fcfc560c2cfca). This is the exception documented by #20153.

Replaced the direct ASM visitor with ordinary Byte Buddy advice in [`a230473`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/commit/a230473d861de9ee22834e9d06acc1a1728d80e1). It stages nodes at terminal cache-constructor entry and attaches them at `TopologyRefreshTask` constructor exit before scheduling, since this Byte Buddy version cannot read uninitialized `this` at constructor entry.

Removed the manual dual-carrier registration in [`7ccf5c5`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/commit/7ccf5c54238c4c7f56e93a793640c0796bcd15c4) after the stable baseline eliminated the beta provider type. There is no remaining code that needs the comment.

Removed the beta-specific comment and support path in [`7ccf5c5`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/commit/7ccf5c54238c4c7f56e93a793640c0796bcd15c4) by raising the minimum to stable 4.0.0. `JedisSentinelPool` instrumentation remains for the stable range.

Removed the `:muzzle` compile-only dependency in [`7ccf5c5`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/commit/7ccf5c54238c4c7f56e93a793640c0796bcd15c4) together with `@NoMuzzle`; it had been needed only to compile that annotation.

threads.body: [General] The public zero-argument `DefaultJedisSocketFactory` constructor is not matched. In supported Jedis 4.x/5.x it has an empty body and retains the known default `hostAndPort`, so passing that factory to a client leaves the virtual-field target unset and stable telemetry omits `server.address`. Instrument this constructor by reading its initialized field, and add a direct-client assertion for this path.

replies.body:
Addressed in 0867c7faf11cc0d2bb22ff01bc79a260615c272b.

Analysis: Jedis 4.0 and 5.1 initialize `hostAndPort` to the default target in the zero-argument constructor. The existing constructor matchers skipped that signature. The new advice reads the initialized field on exit, and the direct-client test routes the socket to the test container without changing that logical target.

Upsides: Stable telemetry now records the default `server.address`. The test covers both old and stable database semantic conventions.

Downsides: This adds one constructor advice and a test-only forwarding socket factory.

Addressed in f12c309a462d097d4d6f01dcf75a0b5535b77ec6.

Analysis: Repository instructions prohibit direct edits to `docs/instrumentation-list.yaml`. The nightly metadata workflow derives this target range from the Muzzle configuration, so this commit restores the generated file to its base content.

Upsides: The pull request now changes the Muzzle source of truth only. The metadata workflow can regenerate the documentation after merge.

Downsides: The checked-in instrumentation list will keep the previous range until the nightly workflow updates it.

threads.body: [Testing] This new sharded-provider propagation path has no end-to-end coverage. The Jedis 4.0 provider creates its connection pools inside `initialize(List)`, so a matcher or scope regression here would silently make sharded commands report the selected peer instead of the ordered configured shard list; the current tests exercise direct, pooled, cluster, and Sentinel paths but never construct a sharded provider. Please add a stable/legacy command test whose configured shard list differs from the selected peer.

replies.body:
Addressed in db68a87e46f2d9296cb9ea053527d489fe0beea6.

Analysis: Jedis 5.1 lazily sends two CLIENT SETINFO commands when the selected shard connection opens and does not send QUIT when the provider closes. The test now warms that exact shard before clearing telemetry and asserts the configured target on the next SET command before close. The Jedis 5.1 suites set testLatestDeps so cleanup trace counts remain deterministic.

Upsides: The sharded configured-target test now covers Jedis 4.0 and 5.1 in both semantic-convention modes without depending on version-specific connection setup spans.

Downsides: The test sends one warm-up command and branches on the existing later-dependency test flag.

threads.body: [Testing] The mapped-client case proves span attributes use the configured host, but it does not verify the PR's corresponding metric behavior. The existing `assertDurationMetric` helper only checks the metric attribute keys (`DbClientMetricsTestUtil.java:40-43`), so metrics could still report the connected peer without any test failing. Please assert the mapped operation's metric point has `server.address=redis.internal` and `server.port=6380`.

replies.body:
Addressed in ac2be24a3ad374d6670ecf035b56b4237d67ddd6.

Analysis: The shared duration metric helper verifies only the attribute keys, so it cannot distinguish configured target values from connected peer values. The mapped-client test now selects the SET metric point and checks its server.address and server.port values.

Upsides: This directly protects the configured target values on operation duration metrics and ties the assertion to the mapped SET command.

Downsides: The stable semantic-convention test performs one additional metric export wait.

threads.body:
I think you don't need to call clear since it gets called before each test anyway.
Above you are asserting for 1 trace, here you could wait for 2. I suspect that this is not going to run stably since the `waitAndAssertTraces` will fail if it gets more traces than expected.
